F-c, the per-paper principal organism. Each paper gets a `principal_organism` decided once, at inclusion. It is a normalize_species key: the single organism the title names, or else the single organism the abstract names, with comparison mentions of the target removed first. It is "" when the deciding source names no recognised organism, or more than one. An in_planta-route sentence that names no organism inherits the principal. If the principal is not the target, and that includes "", the sentence gets GRADE_NONE. Three things are left alone: the review route (species.py:961 already requires the sentence itself to name the target), sentences that name the target or another organism, and aggregate_species. The principal is never the claim's species, so B3 holds. The new veto is OR'd onto the existing paper_other/span_other veto at species.py:941. Because it only removes credit it is monotone fail-closed: an in_planta grade can only become none.

F-a (BIO-745B-2), participant citations verified. A participant the model cites (it has valid evidence_ids) keeps the label 'model_citation' only when one of its strict name variants, or a per-paper alias of one, occurs as a whole token in at least one span that participant cites. Otherwise the participant is kept but labelled 'model_citation_unverified', and the claim cannot be target_species_supported: it becomes species_ambiguous and stays a lead. It is used for this check only and never for sentence credit, so it cannot add recall. The demotion fires only where aggregate_species would otherwise return TSS (an in_planta or review grade is present).
